content: The title of the page should be formatted as (Disease name) symptoms, with only the first letter of the title capitalized. The primary objective of this page is to describe the typical symptoms that a patient reports. It is important to note that symptoms are distinct from signs, which are clinical findings observed by physicians. At the top of the edit box, include the following elements: the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template that you created at the beginning. When creating links within WikiDoc, enclose key terms in brackets to link them to other pages. Ensure that the links are as specific as possible. For instance, if a sentence includes the term anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to the page for anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. Follow the formatting and capitalization guidelines outlined in the provided template. The name of the disease should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. Overview Section The overview section must include the name of the disease in the first sentence. The purpose of this section is to summarize the history and symptoms page in a few sentences. This section can be identical to the history and symptoms segment on the overview page. Template for Writing First Sentences: Examples of how to begin the section should be provided. Additional Sentences: Examples of how to elaborate on the content should also be included. Preferred Template Statements If the disease has a hallmark symptom, use statements such as: The hallmark of [disease] is [symptom]. A positive history of [symptom] is suggestive of [disease]. The most common symptoms of [disease] include [symptom] and [symptom]. If the disease has multiple equally recognizable symptoms, use statements such as: Symptoms of [disease] include [symptom] and [symptom]. If it is appropriate to distinguish between common and less common symptoms, use the following format: On the overview page, use full sentences: Common symptoms of [disease] include [symptom] and [symptom]. Less common symptoms of [disease] include [symptom] and [symptom]. On the history and symptoms microchapter, use bullet points: Common symptoms of [disease] include: [Symptom] [Symptom] If symptoms are usually absent, use statements such as: The majority of patients with [disease] are asymptomatic. History Section In this section, describe the key components of the patient’s history that require particular attention. Include relevant details from the patient’s past medical history, family history, social history (e.g., occupation, alcohol use with amount and frequency, smoking, drug use), and allergies. This section is not intended to describe the natural history of the disease or provide a historical perspective. Common Symptoms Section List the common symptoms that a patient may experience. Less Common Symptoms Section List the less common symptoms that a patient may experience.
